{{About|the original series episode list|the sequel series episode list|List of Naruto: Shippuden episodes{{!}}List of ''Naruto: Shippuden'' episodes}}
[[File:Naruto logo.svg|alt=The Naruto franchise logo, where there is a yellow to orange gradient in each letter.|250px|frameless|right]]
''[[Naruto (TV series)|Naruto]]'' is an [[anime]] television series based on [[Masashi Kishimoto]]'s manga series of the [[Naruto|same name]]. It follows [[Naruto Uzumaki]], a young [[ninja]] who seeks recognition from his peers and dreams of becoming the Hokage, the leader of the village. The series was directed by Hayato Date, and produced by [[Pierrot (company)|Pierrot]] and [[TV Tokyo]].<ref name="JapanSeason1">{{Cite web|url=http://mediaarts-db.jp/an/anime_series/8019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211235556/http://mediaarts-db.jp/an/anime_series/8019 |archive-date=February 11, 2017 |script-title=ja:NARUTO-ナルト- |language=ja |website=Media Arts Database |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |url-status=dead }}</ref>  The episodes are based on the first [[List of Naruto chapters (Part I)#Volume list|twenty-seven]] volumes in Part I of the manga, while some episodes feature original, self-contained storylines.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.animesays.com/list/naruto/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220180640/http://www.animesays.com/list/naruto/ |archive-date=February 20, 2016 |title=Naruto Filler & Episode List – AnimeSays |publisher=AnimeSays |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The 220 episodes that constitute the series were aired between October 3, 2002, and February 8, 2007, on TV Tokyo in [[Japan]].<ref name="JapanSeason1"/> The English version of the series was released in North America by [[Viz Media]], and began airing on September 10, 2005, on [[Cartoon Network]]'s [[Toonami]] programming block in the [[United States]].<ref name="EnglishSeason1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/tv/naruto/1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305141632/http://www.ign.com/tv/naruto/1 |archive-date=March 5, 2016 |title= Naruto: Season 1 |publisher=IGN |url-status=dead }}</ref> On September 20, 2008, Cartoon Network ended its Toonami block, but the channel continued sporadically airing episodes of ''Naruto'' in the time slots originally occupied by Toonami's programming until January 31, 2009, when episode 209, the last episode to air in the United States was shown, due to the closure of [[Toonami Jetstream]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2008-09-20/cartoon-network-to-reportedly-end-toonami-tonight |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161112024912/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2008-09-20/cartoon-network-to-reportedly-end-toonami-tonight |archive-date=November 12, 2016 |title=Cartoon Network to End Toonami on September 20 (Updated) |publisher=[[Anime News Network]] |date=September 20, 2008}}</ref><!-- NOTE TO EDITORS: Episode 210 DID NOT AIR on Cartoon Network in North America - Anime News Network is incorrect, and the ANN Encyclopedia is NOT a reliable source! ANN's cited source, the November 2009 issue of Shonen Jump, did provide an airdate for episode 210, but it also gave a disclaimer along the lines of "Episode airdates and titles are not fixed, and are subject to change without notice" Further changes stating that episode 210 aired without a RELIABLE SOURCE (not the ANN Encyclopedia) will be reverted! -->

On March 23, 2009, Viz stated that they were still dubbing new episodes and intended to see them aired on television.<ref name="ANNMoreNaruto">{{Cite web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-03-23/viz-confirms-plans-to-present-new-dubbed-naruto |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114142722/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-03-23/viz-confirms-plans-to-present-new-dubbed-naruto |archive-date=November 14, 2016 |title=Viz Confirms Plans to Present New Dubbed Naruto |publisher=[[Anime News Network]] |date=March 23, 2009}}</ref><ref name="watchnarutoepisodesonline">{{Cite web|url=http://www.narutogetonline.com/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113181020/http://www.narutogetonline.com/ |archive-date=November 13, 2016 |title=Naruto Get Online|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ultimately, the final eleven episodes of the series never aired in the United States, but they were collected on DVD by Viz, which was released on September 22, 2009.<ref name="Naruto16"/> The remaining eleven episodes of the English version aired on [[YTV (Canadian TV channel)|YTV]]'s [[Bionix (TV programming block)|Bionix]] programming block in [[Canada]] from October 25 to December 6, 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-12-02/1st-naruto-anime-finale-premieres-on-canada-ytv |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114211617/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-12-02/1st-naruto-anime-finale-premieres-on-canada-ytv |archive-date=November 14, 2016 |title=1st Naruto Anime's Finale Premieres on Canada's YTV |publisher=[[Anime News Network]] |date=December 2, 2009}}</ref> [[Adult Swim]]'s relaunched Toonami block reran the first 52 episodes in a completely uncut format from December 1, 2012, to November 30, 2013. After the 52nd episode, the series was removed from the schedule rotation to make room for its successor series, ''[[Naruto: Shippuden]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2012-11-22/naruto-to-run-uncut-on-adult-swim-toonami-block |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114211617/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2012-11-22/naruto-to-run-uncut-on-adult-swim-toonami-block |archive-date=November 14, 2016 |title=Naruto to run uncut on Adult Swim's Toonami Block |publisher=[[Anime News Network]] |date=November 11, 2012}}</ref>
